claim.section: 8.4.5.1 Local and global names, rule 3) b)
claim.pdf_says:
b)  Otherwise, if source element A is contained within another source element, the referenced item is:
        1.  The item in source element A if the name is declared in source element A.
        2.  The item in the containing source element if the name is not declared in source element A and ...
claim.markdown_says:
b) Otherwise, if source element A is contained within another source element, the referenced item is:

   1\. The item in source element A if the name is declared in source element A.

   2\. The item in the containing source element if the name is not declared in source element A and ...
claim.note: The printed sub-items 1. and 2. are nested under b); the markdown sets them at the same indentation as a) and b), detaching them from their parent b).
claim.why_it_matters: Flattening the nesting makes items 1. and 2. look like siblings of a) and b) instead of the two cases of rule b), obscuring the name-resolution order.

verdict.reasoning: On printed page 140 (sheet 116), items 1. and 2. sit one indent level deeper than a) and b) under rule 3) b) of 8.4.5.1. The markdown (page-140.md lines 36-42) gives a), b), 1\. and 2\. the same 3-space indent, so the claim describes the difference correctly. The difference is still only indentation. The markdown keeps every word in the same order. b) still ends with 'the referenced item is:', which items 1. and 2. complete. Their numbering style (1., 2.) also differs from the a)/b) style, so a reader cannot take them for siblings of a) and b), and the name-resolution order is unchanged. No content is missing, misplaced or changed, so this is a formatting difference that does not change meaning.
